Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Aussie players are in a huddle, where Sophie Molineux is giving them a last-minute pep talk before they take on the field. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are the two openers for India Women. Darcie Brown will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
…THE RUN CHASE…

All eyes on the chase - Now, chasing 134, India Women will be confident of getting the job done, but Australia Women will surely come hard with the ball. So, who are you backing to take a 1-0 lead in the series? We’ll find out soon. Stay tuned as we bring you live updates from the second innings shortly.

India run riot with the ball - India Women were exceptional with the ball, consistently taking wickets and building pressure with their brilliant ground fielding. Arundhati Reddy was the standout, claiming four wickets, while Renuka Singh Thakur and Sree Charani supported brilliantly with two wickets each, maintaining relentless pressure throughout. Kranti Gaud and Deepti Sharma chipped in with one wicket apiece, completing a stellar bowling performance from the visitors.

Australia's batting meltdown - Australia Women endured a disappointing batting performance, being bowled out for just 133 in their allotted 20 overs. Sent in to bat, they lost both openers inside the Powerplay and struggled to build any significant partnerships, with wickets tumbling at regular intervals. Georgia Wareham top-scored with a gritty 30, while Litchfield and Perry contributed useful 20s each but were unable to convert their starts into a match-defining innings. At 87/5 at the halfway stage, it seemed possible Australia could push past 170, but the lower order collapsed spectacularly, leaving them well short of a competitive total.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin now! The Indian players make their way out to the middle through the smoke and fireworks and take up the fielding positions. Beth Mooney and Georgia Voll are the two openers for Australia Women. Renuka Singh Thakur has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. A slip in place. Let's play...

UPDATE - 8.20 am GMT (1.50 pm IST) - The start of the game has been slightly delayed due to the earlier drizzle. However, the weather is clear now, and we hope it stays like this and we get a full game.

The skipper of Australia Women - Sophie Molineux says there is a strong rivalry between the two sides and believes it will be an exciting series. She adds that there is no better place to begin than the SCG. Molineux notes that conditions could be a bit slippery, but the team is prepared to adapt and aims to post a competitive total on the board. She concludes by confirming that the squad is injury-free.

The captain of India Women - Harmanpreet Kaur says that, looking at the overcast conditions and chances of rain, it is better to bowl first. Adds that wherever they go, they always get huge support. Says that they always enjoy playing against Australia and are looking forward to it.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Kranti Gaud, Sree Charani, Renuka Singh Thakur.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Beth Mooney (WK), Georgia Voll, Phoebe Litchfield, Ellyse Perry, Ashleigh Gardner, Georgia Wareham, Annabel Sutherland, Nicola Carey, Sophie Molineux (C), Kim Garth, Darcie Brown.
TOSS - Harmanpreet Kaur from India has won the toss and opted to BOWL first.
UPDATE - 7.48 am GMT (1.18 pm IST) - The toss was scheduled to take place by now, but it has been officially delayed due to a light drizzle, with the umpires standing by under umbrellas.

Heavyweights collide -  With two world-class sides set to clash, expect a fiercely competitive encounter and another thrilling chapter in this growing rivalry. Who will strike first and take a 1-0 lead in the series? We’ll find out soon. Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned.

Confident India eye strong start -  India, on the other hand, arrive brimming with confidence. They recently swept Sri Lanka 5-0 in a T20I series and also clinched the 50-over World Cup title a few months ago, underlining their rise as a dominant force. Led by the experienced Harmanpreet Kaur, India’s batting is powered by the elegant Smriti Mandhana, the dynamic Shafali Verma, and the dependable Jemimah Rodrigues. Their bowling attack will lean on Renuka Singh Thakur, Shreyanka Patil, Sree Charani, and Kranti Gaud, while versatile performers like Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh, Amanjot Kaur, and Sneh Rana offer valuable all-round strength.

Molineux takes charge -  The T20I reins now pass to Sophie Molineux, who begins her first assignment as captain. With experienced campaigners like Tahlia McGrath and Ashleigh Gardner serving as vice-captains, Australia boast a balanced and formidable unit. The batting lineup features the explosive talents of Beth Mooney, Ellyse Perry, Phoebe Litchfield, Grace Harris, and emerging star Georgia Voll. In the bowling department, the pace and precision of Darcie Brown, Kim Garth, and Nicola Carey will be key, while all-rounders Georgia Wareham and Annabel Sutherland add depth and versatility. Australia will be keen to make a strong statement at home and draw first blood.

Healy’s farewell tour -  Australia enter the contest following their ODI World Cup campaign in October, where they bowed out in the semi-finals against India. Since then, veteran skipper Alyssa Healy has stepped away from the shortest format and is set to bring the curtain down on her illustrious international career at the end of this multi-format series, continuing to lead the side in the ODIs and the standalone Test.

Sydney showdown kicks off the series - Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 1st T20I in the three-match series between Australia Women and India Women from the iconic Sydney Cricket Ground. Both teams return to action after a considerable break and will be eager to fine-tune their combinations ahead of the T20 World Cup in June. With plenty at stake and momentum to build, this series promises to be a crucial preparatory phase for two of the game’s heavyweights.
…MATCHDAY…

A grand finale to the summer - India, the ODI champions, have touched down in Australia. Two powerhouses of women's cricket will clash across all three formats in a fitting finale to the Australian summer of international cricket. It promises to be intense and closely fought. This tour is not a set of separate bilateral series. It is one combined, points-based contest featuring three T20Is, three ODIs and a one-off Test. Every match contributes to a single table, and the team with more points at the end of the 7 games will lift the trophy. New to the multi-format system? We have got you covered. In the T20Is and ODIs, a win earns two points while a loss earns none. A no result or an abandoned match gives one point to each side. The lone Test carries greater value, with four points for a win and two each in case of a draw. The series begins with the T20Is, an important leg with a World Cup in England coming up in June. The opener will be played at the historic Sydney Cricket Ground. The action will then move to Canberra before concluding in Adelaide. Australia usher in a new era - A new chapter begins for Australia as they return to action for the first time since their World Cup semifinal defeat to India in Navi Mumbai. They step into a transition phase with Sophie Molineux appointed as Australia's all-format captain, while Alyssa Healy is set to hang up her boots at the end of this multi-format series. Molineux's elevation came as a surprise to some, given her recent battles with injuries, but the selectors have backed her to lead the side into its next phase. For now, Sophie will captain the T20I leg against India, with Healy leading the side in the ODIs and the one-off Test before bidding farewell. Ashleigh Gardner and Tahlia McGrath were among the contenders for the role and will serve as deputies to Molineux. Australia once again boast a deep pool of all-rounders. Gardner, Molineux and Harris provide spin options, while Ellyse Perry, McGrath and Annabel Sutherland add seam bowling depth. Perry and Sutherland missed the WPL due to personal reasons, but they enter the series after stints in the Women's National Cricket League, Australia's domestic 50-over competition. Nicola Carey also returns to the side after turning down a central contract in 2023. Her recall follows impactful performances in the WBBL and the WPL. The specialist pace options include Kim Garth, Darcie Brown and Megan Schutt, while Georgia Wareham adds to the spin bowling stocks. There is no place for leggie Alana King, who remained on the bench for the Delhi Capitals in the entirety of the WPL. Georgia Voll, Phoebe Litchfield and Beth Mooney feature in the batting group. Litchfield is returning from a quad injury that ended her WPL campaign early but is expected to be available for the opener. India enter a crucial stretch - India step into a crunch phase of 11 matches. Three games against Australia will be followed by five in South Africa in April and then three more in England just before the World Cup. It is a defining stretch in the lead-up to the global tournament, where they will look to add the T20 title to their ODI World Cup crown. Between the 50-over World Cup and this series, India hosted Sri Lanka for a three-match T20I series in December and completed a 3-0 sweep. Harmanpreet Kaur continues to lead the Women in Blue, with Smriti Mandhana serving as her deputy. The pair anchor the side both tactically and with the bat. Jemimah Rodrigues will carry happy memories from the last time she faced Australia, producing a knock for the ages that propelled India into the final, where they eventually emerged champions. There is firepower at the top in Shafali Verma, while Richa Ghosh provides finishing strength in the lower order. Bharti Fulmali adds further hitting power and returns to the T20I squad for the first time since 2019. Another significant return is Shreyanka Patil, whose last T20I appearance came against Australia at the 2024 T20 World Cup before a lengthy injury layoff. She endured a mixed WPL season during RCB's title-winning campaign, but remains a valuable all-round option. Patil can contribute with the bat, as can Amanjot Kaur, Deepti Sharma, Sneh Rana and Arundhati Reddy. The specialist spin options include the left-arm orthodox duo of Sree Charani and Vaishnavi Sharma, with Sharma impressing in her debut series against Sri Lanka. The pace attack will be led by Renuka Singh Thakur and Kranti Gaud, completing a squad built for a demanding run of fixtures. Form (Last 5 completed T20Is, most recent first) - Australia - WWWWW | India - WWWWW. What does history suggest? History favours Australia in this rivalry. They have won four of their five multi-match bilateral women's T20I series against India, including each of the last three. The only time India claimed a T20I series win over Australia came in January 2016, on Australian soil.  At the Sydney Cricket Ground, the hosts have an equally imposing record. Australia are unbeaten in women's T20Is at the venue, winning all four matches played there so far. India, however, will draw confidence from their tour game against the Governor General XI at North Sydney Oval, where a convincing win helped them settle in ahead of the series opener. Recent trends at the SCG - In the last Big Bash League season, three of the four night games at the venue were won by the chasing side. Of the 56 wickets that fell during the 2025/26 BBL at the SCG, 42 were picked by fast bowlers, suggesting the seamers could have a major influence on the opening fixture. It is all set up for an intriguing opener in what is a blockbuster series between two sides that pack plenty of punch. Who are you backing to land the first punch?
